note: The registry of every annotation Ipsissima reads. No new syntax: every key rides in Argdown's own front matter and {data} blocks, or in a source file's YAML front matter. tests/test_profile.py holds this file to what the checker and the app actually read.

defaults.summary: Claim metadata declared once for every claim that does not set its own (usually `chapter`); `reviewed` here records a person's pass over the whole map.

contentions.summary: The text's stated theses, added to the computed apex. Only the author's own.

text-provenance.summary: Declares that the manuscript itself was machine-generated; shown beside the title.

author.summary: Who drew a survey map (a map with no source text).

date.summary: When a survey map was drawn.

mechanism.summary: The causal chain the text asserts.

generated.summary: A model wrote the map; the checker may correct its fidelity markers.

draft.summary: The text is still being written; findings about unfinishedness become observations.

aim.summary: fit: what the text says; appropriation: the best philosophy in it.

unit.summary: Which sense of the words, or which view is held.

strength.summary: How much better than their words the author is assumed to be.

chapter.summary: The source file the claim reads, relative to the source root.

section.summary: The heading in that file the claim belongs to.

source.summary: A quotation pinning a claim whose own text is a summary; verified like any quotation.

echoes.summary: Where else the text states the claim -- its thesis announced in the abstract, say -- as the author's words. Verified like any quotation; never pins the claim, which stays where it is argued.

pinpoint.summary: Where a reader finds it in print: p. 12, pp. 34, 36, [50].

line.summary: The line in the chapter the claim is placed at, where no quotation places it.

fidelity.summary: How far the claim's own text stands from the author's words.

warrant.summary: Why a departure (interpretation, imputation) is allowed.

note.summary: What the notation cannot carry: the limitation, the reading followed, the road not taken.

reviewed.summary: The date a person reviewed the claim. Never set by a model.

causes.summary: The causal step(s) the claim states.

constitutes.summary: The constitutive relation(s) the claim states: what makes a whole up, never walked as a step (since 1.11).

uses.summary: Which premises the step uses; required where a structure has two or more steps.

formalization.summary: The line's logical form, in NLTK syntax.

formalized.summary: The stamp of the words the formula was read against, written by a person with --stamp.

isGroup.summary: Argdown's own: the heading groups its claims.

tags.reported: a view the text sets out but does not hold
tags.conceded: something the author grants tells against them
tags.contested: an objection voiced in the text that is not the author's view
tags.authority: a proposition whose force comes from its source, not its content
tags.obiter: said in a judgment, but not a necessary step to the disposal
tags.crux: a claim the reconstructor settled by choosing among live readings
tags.appraisal: the reconstructor's own reading of the text against the world

levels.summary: Levels of social complexity, top first.

ordering.type: composition | space | authority | scale | sequence | systems | mixed | unstated, or {kind, pinpoint}
ordering.summary: What kind of ordering the levels are; the reconstructor's reading unless a pinpoint shows where the text says it (since 1.10).

within.summary: Each level's parent, where the levels nest: a tree, siblings side by side within their parent (since 1.10).

form.summary: A cycle of reproduction and transformation: not asked where it starts or what it is for, and whatever its loops pass through counts as reached. Also on each chain (since 1.11).

settles.summary: On a cycle: whether the text says it comes to rest (since 1.11).

goal.summary: What the chain is for: to explain why and how, to find what to do, to predict, or to attribute responsibility. Also on each chain (since 1.13).

contrast.summary: The foil the question sets: why this, rather than what. Also on each chain (since 1.13).

keys.label: string
keys.general: a state id of this kind: the general claim, of which the kind's other states are cases (since 1.7)

kinds.summary: Kinds of state that recur across cases; states of one kind are never walked as one (since 1.6).

keys.label: string
keys.question: string
keys.roles: map of state id to a role or list of roles: the role the state plays in this chain
keys.form: chain | cycle: this chain's own form (since 1.11)

chains.summary: Several chains the text sets out, each answering its own question (since 1.5).

keys.label: string
keys.actor: an actor id, or (since 1.12) a list of them: a relation or a doing of several actors together; may be left out where `levels` places a process with no owner (since 1.11)
keys.status: actual | possible | open: whether the state is actual, a possibility the text sets out, or what the text says cannot be specified in advance (since 1.12)
keys.aspect: quantity | activity | development | event | condition: what kind of occurrence the state is, from the text's own grammar (since 1.11)
keys.role: intervention | condition | outcome, or a list of them (condition and lists since 1.1)
keys.part_of: a state id: the whole this state is a part, facet or instance of (since 1.2)
keys.levels: a list of levels: the levels a state holds at, when more than its actor's; drawn across them (since 1.4)
keys.kind: a kind id: the declared kind this state is a case of (since 1.6)
keys.measures: a state id: the state this one is a measure, indicator or estimate of -- a reading of it, never walked as its cause (since 1.9)
keys.method: string: how that measure is taken, in the text's words (since 1.9)

sign.summary: + raises, - lowers, "0" a finding of no effect, which decides which alternative follows (since 1.2).

basis.summary: What the text offers for the step.

period.summary: When the step holds, in the text's words anchored to an event: during culling, after it ended (since 1.8).

on.summary: Whether the step moves the level of its `to` (the default) or its trend: slows a rise, speeds a fall (since 1.8); or (since 1.11) makes or unmakes it (being, + or -), maintains or erodes it (persistence, + or -), or changes what kind of thing it is (character, with sign: which); or (since 1.12) opens or closes the possibility of it (possibility, + or -).

given.summary: Conditions the text states, in its words, or (since 1.8) a declared state and the value it has.

selects.summary: A selection link: who ends up on each side, not an effect.

hedged.summary: The text puts the step as a possibility.

chain.type: chain id or list of chain ids
chain.summary: Which declared chain(s) the step belongs to (since 1.5).

jointly.type: state id or list of state ids
jointly.summary: The step holds only together with these states: a joint cause (since 1.4).

unless.type: state id or list of state ids
unless.summary: The step holds unless these states hold: a blocker, walked as a cause of the opposite sign (since 1.8).

despite.type: state id or list of state ids
despite.summary: The step held although these states acted against it: a blocker that failed, reported and not walked (since 1.8).

regime.summary: The regime the step holds in, in the text's words: a dose, a place, a model. Routes are composed only within one regime (since 1.8).

threshold.summary: The threshold the step acts past, in the text's words: the step is not a monotone rise or fall (since 1.8).

share.summary: How much of the step runs by its `via` route: all of it (the default), most, part, or none of it (since 1.8).

size.type: string or {value, unit, ci, versus, at}
size.summary: The magnitude the text gives for the step, quoted: an effect size, with its interval, comparison and time (since 1.8).

via.type: state id or list of state ids
via.summary: The finer route the text opens this step into, in order: the step IS that route, walked once (since 1.8).

modifies.type: {by, effect, period}, or a list of them
modifies.summary: A state that moderates the step: `effect` strengthens, weakens or reverses it, or -- "0" -- the text finds it does not moderate it. The moderator is linked by the step, never walked as a cause (since 1.9).

necessary.summary: The step's `to` holds only where its `from` does: "only if". Drawn "needed for", not "raises" (since 1.9).

sufficient.summary: `true`: the cause, with any `jointly` co-causes, brings the effect about on its own. `false`: the text says it is not enough on its own (since 1.9).

design.summary: The design of the evidence for the step, in the text's words; these values are read, others kept as written. `illustration` is a hypothetical case, shaded as asserted (since 1.9).

attribution.summary: The type of causing the step attributes, after Stone (1989): purposeful or not, intended or not, guided through another agent, or a web with no single locus; `by` names the actor whose action or intention it is (since 1.9).

measured_by.type: state id or list of state ids
measured_by.summary: The measure the step's evidence is read from: a state with `measures`. A step into that measure other than from what it measures is a bias that bears on the evidence, drawn as an undercut (since 1.9).

stance.summary: On a #reported or #contested step: whether the text sets out the view to reject it or leaves it unjudged. A report the text endorses is a claim in its own voice, not a stance (since 1.9).

association.summary: The text reports that the two go together and does not say one brings the other about: drawn without a head, never walked; the census names any common cause drawn (since 1.13).

scope.summary: Whether the step is about a particular case or a general relation between kinds or variables (since 1.13).

from.summary: What makes the whole up, wholly or partly.

to.summary: The whole: a state, or an actor -- a group or a system that the ongoing states constitute.

extent.summary: Whether it constitutes part of the whole or all of it.

whole.summary: How the whole stands to what constitutes it: no more than their sum; dependent on their organisation; nothing but them; or (since 1.12) each making the other.

basis.summary: What the text offers: as for a step, or an account's judgement, or a definition.

under.summary: The account under which the relation holds, in the text's words: a thick account of race, the orthodox account of class.

stance.summary: On a #reported or #contested claim, as for a step.

constitutes.summary: A constitutive relation (since 1.11): what a whole is made up of, carried by a claim as a step is. Never walked, never composed with steps, never drawn as an arrow; cycles are allowed. A pair may be related both causally and constitutively.

licence.summary: An SPDX identifier where there is one.

abstract.summary: The text's own abstract, shown on the orientation panel.

voice.summary: For a wholly dramatised text: whose voice the mapped argument is in.

facts.summary: For a judgment: the facts of the case.

attribution.summary: For a pasted text: whose it is.

zotero.summary: The Zotero attachment key the text was converted from.

source_markup.back_matter: the first heading of References, Notes, Bibliography and their kin; kept in the file, never quoted as argument
source_markup.project_file: chapters: a list of files, optionally grouped under `part:`; Quarto's `book: chapters:` is read the same way

folded: runs of whitespace, the non-breaking space among them
single, double, curly and straight quotation marks and guillemets, all as one
en and em dashes, as a hyphen
the ellipsis character, as three stops
